title: Does Inference Temperature Actually Reduce Cross-Model Homogeneity?

original_idea.body:
# Does Inference Temperature Actually Reduce Cross-Model Homogeneity?

**Problem:** Prior work claims temperature/top-p does not mitigate monoculture, but most evidence is on intra-model repetition. Whether raising temperature reduces INTER-model homogeneity on safety-relevant tasks is underexplored.

**Direction:** For a fixed prompt set, sweep temperature across several open models and measure inter-model homogeneity at each temperature. Separate RLHF-tuned vs base models.

**Why it matters:** If temperature can't break inter-model agreement, deployment-time mitigations are illusory.

**Relevant context:** RLHF effects on diversity (arXiv:2310.06452); Artificial Hivemind.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible deployment-relevance (temperature as illusory mitigation) but indirect catastrophic-risk link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure temperature sweep with embedding similarity; very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped sweep with clear inter-model homogeneity metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Externally doable but a knob labs could trivially sweep; incremental.

novelty.reasoning: Temperature-does-not-help claim already exists; inter-model dimension only mildly new.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Prior work already claims temperature does not mitigate monoculture; inter-model slice marginal.
